name: purgeRenderCaches
description: Ask the renderers and GPU process a Nexus client uses to drop their caches by sending them a memory-pressure level and then NONE. Nothing is terminated or frozen. Rate-limited per target in the host. Returns { purged: string[], throttled: string[], guestProcesses, agentTabProcesses, gpuProcesses, workingSetTrim?, skipped? }. Present only in a build that has an implementation and, for a debug build, only when started with --velloc-memory-purge-for-testing: such a host lists appInfo.purgeRenderCaches in the manifest's primitives; any other answers NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Within 60 s of the browser process starting it answers APP_INFO_STARTUP_GRACE; a debug build started with that switch is outside the grace and also lists appInfo.purgeRenderCaches.forTesting, which promises no more than that. A release build always purges but keeps the grace, switch or not.

inputs.name: targets
inputs.description: Any of "guest" (the Nexus page's renderers in every window), "gpu" (the GPU process), "agentTabs" (renderers of session-tagged tabs). Default ["guest", "gpu"]. An unknown name is invalid_args.

inputs.name: level
inputs.description: "moderate" or "critical" (default). An unknown level is invalid_args.

inputs.name: trimWorkingSet
inputs.description: true: also ask the host to empty its processes' working sets shortly after. Honoured only by a host that lists appInfo.purgeRenderCaches.trimWorkingSet; the reply's workingSetTrim is then "scheduled", "below_spec" or "unsupported", and is absent otherwise.

inputs.name: onlyWhenAppInactive
inputs.description: true: do nothing while the foreground window belongs to the browser process, and answer skipped: "app_active" with empty lists and zero counts. Honoured only by a host that lists appInfo.purgeRenderCaches.onlyWhenAppInactive. The skip is decided before targets and level are resolved, so a request carrying an unknown one is answered with the skip, not invalid_args, while a host window is in the foreground.
